# TerminusDB MCP

Model Context Protocol endpoint for TerminusDB. One endpoint, six workflow tools:
schema → orient, query → retrieve and verify, write → change data, git → version,
admin → operate, plugins → extend.

## Endpoints

- HTTP (enterprise): `POST /api/mcp` — stateless streamable HTTP, one JSON-RPC 2.0
  request per POST. `GET /llms.txt` serves this document.
- stdio (community): `terminusdb mcp` — newline-delimited JSON-RPC on stdin/stdout
  against the local binary store. No port is opened.

Client registration:

    claude mcp add terminusdb -- terminusdb mcp

    .vscode/mcp.json:
    { "servers": { "terminusdb": { "command": "terminusdb", "args": ["mcp"] } } }

    claude_desktop_config.json:
    { "mcpServers": { "terminusdb": { "command": "terminusdb", "args": ["mcp"] } } }

    Enterprise HTTP:
    { "url": "https://<host>/api/mcp", "headers": { "Authorization": "Bearer <token>" } }

`terminusdb mcp` is configured by environment:

    TERMINUSDB_SERVER_DB_PATH    store location — default ~/.terminusdb,
                                 auto-initialized on first run
    TERMINUSDB_INDEXER_BACKEND   semantic indexer — `vectorlink` enables the
                                 embedded engine; default `none` disables
                                 search (no webserver needed — works on stdio)
    TERMINUSDB_MEMORY_PASSWORD   set to run an ephemeral in-memory store;
                                 the value is the admin password (empty → root)

## Auth

HTTP: basic auth, `Authorization: API_KEY <key>`, or `Authorization: Bearer <JWT>`
(OIDC discovery on the enterprise build). stdio: runs as the invoking local user —
no token.

## Resources

`"org/db"` (default branch main), `"org/db/local/branch/<name>"`,
`"org/db/local/commit/<id>"`. `graph_type`: `"instance"` | `"schema"`.

## Calling

    {"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":1,"method":"tools/call",
     "params":{"name":"<tool>","arguments":{"action":"…",…}}}

Response: `result.structuredContent` carries the payload; `result.content` mirrors
it as text. Tool failure is `isError:true` — never a JSON-RPC error. Malformed
requests (bad JSON, missing or non-string `method`) do get JSON-RPC errors
(-32700/-32600/-32601/-32602); a request with no `id` is a notification and gets
no response. Transport-level failure (calls failing with "Not connected" or
similar) means the client lost the server process — restart it; no tool call can
reconnect for you.

## Tools

Every tool takes `action` plus its own arguments; errors are `isError:true` results
with `structuredContent.{error,message,hint}` — the hint names the corrected call.

### schema — read the data model

    {"action":"summary","resource":"org/db"}          → counts, classes, data_version
    {"action":"full","resource":"org/db"}             → all class frames
    {"action":"frame","resource":"org/db","class":"Person"}
    {"action":"frame",...,"format":"jsonschema"}      → JSON Schema draft-07
    {"action":"vocab","resource":"org/db"}            → @context/prefixes
    {"action":"contract","resource":"org/db"}         → compact class shapes
    {"action":"datatypes"}                            → every valid type spelling —
        no resource needed. `datatypes` lists base types ("xsd:string",
        "xsd:integer", "xdd:coordinate", ...), `schema_types` the document
        @type spellings (Class, TaggedUnion, Enum, Foreign), `families` the
        range wrappers (Optional, Set, List, Array, Table, Cardinality).
        A property range is a datatype string or a family wrapper:
        {"name":"xsd:string"} or {"nick":{"@type":"Optional","@class":"xsd:string"}}
        — there is no "@type":"String" object form. `annotations` lists the
        recognized class metadata keys (@key, @inherits, @subdocument,
        @abstract, @unfoldable, @shared, @metadata, @documentation); every
        non-@ member of a Class doc is a property slot — "comment",
        "description", "title" are NOT annotations, they become properties
        whose range is their string value (usually a schema error).

### query — retrieve and verify (read-only)

    {"action":"document","path":"org/db","id":"Person/x"}
    {"action":"document","path":"org/db","type":"City","count":10}
    {"action":"document","path":"org/db","type":"City","query":{"name":"Lisbon"}}
        — match by property value; "fields":["name"] projects properties
    {"action":"document",...,"id_only":true}          → ids only
    {"action":"document",...,"format":"embedding"}    → rendered text, not JSON
        — renders each doc through its class's @metadata.embedding template
          (GraphQL query + Handlebars — the same text that gets embedded for
          semantic search). "format":"markdown" renders markdown instead.
          Returns documents:[{id,text}] plus "page": the concatenated page.
          Needs no indexer backend; incompatible with id_only/fields.
    {"action":"woql","path":"org/db","query":<WOQL JSON AST>,"count":5}
        — count caps returned bindings
    {"action":"check","path":"org/db","verb":"insert","documents":<doc|[docs]>}
    {"action":"graphql","path":"org/db","query":"{ Person { name } }","variables":{…}}
    {"action":"search","path":"org/db","kind":"search","q":"lisbon"}
        — "query" is accepted as an alias for "q"
        — kind: search|similar|suggest|duplicates; needs a VectorLink index
    {"action":"history","path":"org/db","id":"Person/x","count":50}
        — flags: created/updated/diff/fast/complete; bounds: before/after/start/count
    {"action":"diff","path":"org/db","before":"<commit>","after":"<commit>","id":"Person/x"}
        — omit id for all changed documents

`query.woql` is read-only — InsertDocument/UpdateDocument/DeleteDocument/
AddTriple/DeleteTriple etc. are rejected with a hint to route through `write`.
WOQL `Get` (file/URL ingest) is rejected on both `query` and `write` — over MCP
there is no upload channel for `post` and `url` would fetch server-side.

`query.check` is the try-before-commit dry run: runs the real write path in a
discarded transaction and reports `{api:valid, api:witnesses, api:embedding}`.
`valid:false` is DATA, not an error — read the witnesses. Run `check` before
every `write` batch — it is free.

### write — change data or schema (every write is a commit)

    {"action":"insert","resource":"org/db","commit_info":{"author":"me","message":"add cities"},
     "documents":[{"@type":"City","name":"Lisbon"}]}
    {"action":"update", ...same shape — replaces documents by @id}
    {"action":"delete","resource":"org/db","commit_info":{...},"id":"City/x"}
        — selectors: id | ids | type | nuke:true
    {"action":"patch","patch":[{"@id":"Person/x","name":{"@op":"SwapValue","@before":"a","@after":"b"}}]}
        — or [{"@op":"Insert","@insert":{…}}]; a list of diff ops
        — SwapValue's @before must equal the stored value exactly ("" is a
          valid @before and matches an empty field); to set a field without
          checking the old value: {"@op":"ForceValue","@after":"b"}
    {"action":"woql","query":<write-capable WOQL AST>}
        — InsertDocument takes the document as a Value/DictionaryTemplate:
        {"@type":"InsertDocument",
         "document":{"@type":"Value","dictionary":{"@type":"DictionaryTemplate",
           "data":[{"@type":"FieldValuePair","field":"@type","value":{"@type":"Value","data":"City"}},
                   {"@type":"FieldValuePair","field":"@id","value":{"@type":"Value","node":"City/Lisbon"}},
                   {"@type":"FieldValuePair","field":"name","value":{"@type":"Value","data":"Lisbon"}}]}},
         "identifier":{"@type":"NodeValue","variable":"id"}}
        — the response's `ids` lists every document the commit actually
          changed (parent→head document diff) — generated ids and changes
          made by raw triple writes are covered too, not just AST-declared
          identifier nodes
    {"action":"graphql","query":"mutation($i:JSON!){_insertDocuments(json:$i)}",
     "variables":{"i":[{doc…}]},"commit_info":{...}}
        — json: takes a JSON variable or JSON string, not an inline object

`commit_info` is mandatory. Returns `{data_version, ids, embedded, not_embedded}`.
Pass `expected_data_version:"branch:<commit>"` to guard against drift — on
conflict, re-read, re-check, rewrite at the new head.

A schema write is an ordinary insert/update with `graph_type:"schema"`. A
class is one document; a property's range is the bare datatype string, NOT a
`{"@id":…,"@type":…}` object — `{"name":{"@type":"String"}}` is never valid:

    {"action":"insert","resource":"org/db","graph_type":"schema","commit_info":{...},
     "documents":[{"@type":"Class","@id":"Employee",
                   "@key":{"@type":"Lexical","@fields":["name"]},
                   "name":"xsd:string",
                   "age":"xsd:integer",
                   "nickname":{"@type":"Optional","@class":"xsd:string"},
                   "aliases":{"@type":"Set","@class":"xsd:string"}}]}

Schema writes (`graph_type:"schema"`) auto-inject `@metadata.embedding` for
classes that lack it when an indexer backend is active — every class becomes
vector-searchable. `indexing:false` opts out; `indexing:{"query","template"}`
overrides the generated query and is stored even with no backend — the
template then renders via `query.document format:"embedding"`, though the
class is not searchable until an indexer runs. The response's `embedded`/
`not_embedded` lists name which classes will and will not be searchable,
with reasons.

### git — version control for data

    {"action":"log","resource":"org/db","count":20}
    {"action":"list_branches","resource":"org/db"}
    {"action":"create_branch","resource":"org/db/local/branch/new","source":"org/db"}
    {"action":"delete_branch","resource":"org/db/local/branch/x",
     "confirm":"permanently delete x"}
    {"action":"merge","resource":"org/db","source":"org/db/local/branch/feature",
     "commit_info":{...}}
        — the other-end ref goes in "source", "to" or "onto" (interchangeable)
    {"action":"squash","resource":"org/db","commit_info":{...},
     "confirm":"rewrite history of main"}
        — rewrites branch history to one commit; confirm-gated like reset
    {"action":"reset","resource":"org/db","to":"<commit-id-or-path>",
     "confirm":"rewrite history of main"}
        — bare commit ids and "org/db/local/commit/<id>" paths both work
    {"action":"rebase","resource":"org/db/local/branch/feature","source":"org/db",
     "commit_info":{...}}
        — replays the resource branch's commits onto the source head

Merge computes the true common ancestor itself — never pass one. Conflicts
return isError with `witnesses` naming the contested document and fields —
`@expected` is the ancestor value, `@found` yours, `@incoming` theirs. Decide
the correct values, then `write` the resolved documents on the target
branch: that commit completes the merge manually. Retrying `merge` re-reports
the same conflict (it is always computed against the shared ancestor).

### admin — operate the server

    {"action":"info"}                                  → version, auth, indexer
    {"action":"list_databases"}
    {"action":"create_database","resource":"org/db","label":"…","comment":"…"}
    {"action":"delete_database","resource":"org/db",
     "confirm":"permanently delete org/db"}
    {"action":"optimize","resource":"org/db"}
    {"action":"index_status","resource":"org/db"}      → indexer backend state (one block per resource)
    {"action":"reindex","resource":"org/db"}
    {"action":"export","resource":"org/db"}            → bundle text in `payload`
    {"action":"import","resource":"org/db","payload":"<bundle text>"}
    {"action":"export","resource":"org/db","path":"/tmp/dump.terminusdb"}   ← stdio only
    {"action":"import","resource":"org/db","path":"/tmp/dump.terminusdb"}   ← stdio only
    {"action":"docs"}                                  → this document

export/import move the bundle as a `payload` string — pass it back to
`import` verbatim (it is not JSON; do not reformat it). `path` reads and
writes files on the server, so it is rejected over HTTP and works on
`terminusdb mcp` only. `import` writes into an existing database —
`create_database` the target first if it is new.
A bundle carries ONE branch's history (main by default) — the export result
lists `branches_not_exported`; export other branches one at a time by
addressing them (`org/db/local/branch/name`), or use git remotes for a
full clone.

## The confirm contract

Irreversible actions require `confirm` echoing the refusal's exact string —
`"permanently delete <resource>"` for deletes (a database `admin/uat`, or a
branch name `x`), `"rewrite history of <branch>"` for resets and squashes.
Try once without it: the error names the literal expected. Applies to:
`admin.delete_database`, `git.delete_branch`, `git.reset`, `git.squash`.

## Data-version discipline

Every `write`/`git` mutation returns `data_version` ("branch:<commit>"). Capture
it; pass `expected_data_version` on the next write to prove you are updating the
head you read. Mismatch → conflict error → re-read, re-check, rewrite.

## Semantic search (GraphRAG)

VectorLink provides vector storage and search; Ollama provides the embeddings —
it is a prerequisite, not an optional extra:

    https://ollama.com/download
    ollama pull hf.co/vectorlink/multilingual-e5-base-GGUF:q8_0
    ollama cp hf.co/vectorlink/multilingual-e5-base-GGUF:q8_0 multilingual-e5-base

Set `TERMINUSDB_INDEXER_BACKEND=vectorlink` before launching `terminusdb mcp` —
the embedded engine runs in-process (no webserver, no separate endpoint).
Schema writes auto-inject embedding metadata; `query.check` reports
`api:will_embed` before you commit. If a class lacks embedding metadata,
`write` reports it in `not_embedded` with the reason.

Changing a class's schema, embedding query or template reindexes every touched
object — on large data products verify impact first (`admin.index_status`,
`git` for a safe branch).

## WOQL cheat-sheet (JSON AST)

    {"@type":"IsA","element":{"@type":"NodeValue","variable":"X"},
     "type":{"@type":"NodeValue","node":"City"}}
    {"@type":"Triple","subject":{...NodeValue/Value...},"predicate":{...},
     "object":{...}}
    {"@type":"And","and":[<query>,...]}  |  {"@type":"Or","or":[...]}
    {"@type":"Select","variables":["X"],"query":<query>}

Discover classes with `schema` action `summary`, property names with `frame` or
`contract`, prefixes with `vocab`.

This document is served at GET /llms.txt on any TerminusDB server and is also
available through the `admin` tool's `docs` action.
